subject: Climate & Environment
title: Landfill Diversion Strategies
description: A fast breakdown of Landfill Diversion Strategies for builders.

hook.text: San Francisco diverts 80% of its waste from landfills. The city aims for zero waste by 2030.

buildup.text: Mandatory composting, recycling, and construction waste sorting form the backbone of the system.

discovery.text: Pay-as-you-throw policies charge residents by the bag — making waste reduction financially rewarding.

twist.text: South Korea charges for food waste by weight. The result: a 30% reduction in food waste.

climax.text: Every city that diverts waste also cuts greenhouse gas emissions from decomposing organic matter.

punchline.text: The best way to deal with waste is to never create it in the first place.

quiz.question: How much waste does San Francisco divert from landfills?

details.summary: Landfill diversion redirects waste away from landfills through recycling, composting, reuse, and waste-to-energy. Cities like San Francisco divert over 80 percent of waste from landfill through aggressive sorting mandates, pay-as-you-throw pricing, and comprehensive composting programs.
details.whyItMatters: Landfills are a major source of methane, a potent greenhouse gas. Diverting waste reduces emissions, conserves resources, and extends the life of existing disposal sites.
takeaways: Top cities divert over 80 percent of waste from landfills
Composting keeps organic waste from producing methane

faq.question: What is pay-as-you-throw?
faq.answer: Pay-as-you-throw charges households based on the volume or weight of trash they produce, rather than a flat fee. Recycling and composting are free or cheaper. This pricing incentivizes waste reduction and sorting, typically cutting landfill waste by 25 to 40 percent.

faq.question: Can any city achieve zero landfill waste?
faq.answer: True zero waste is extremely difficult, but several cities aim for 90 percent diversion or higher. Success requires comprehensive infrastructure for recycling, composting, and reuse, combined with product redesign and producer responsibility legislation.
